documents.title: Office relocation
documents.text:
To: All Staff
From: Hannah Lowe, Operations Manager
Date: January 14

Dear colleagues,
As announced last autumn, our department will move from the Carter Building to the Westgate Tower on the weekend of February 22. Movers will pack all desk contents on Friday afternoon, so please label every box with your name and new floor number. Computers will be transported by the IT team and will be ready for use on Monday morning. Parking permits for the Westgate garage will be distributed next week; those who commute by train may request a transit pass instead. Please note that the new building has no cafeteria, but there are several restaurants within a short walk. I appreciate your cooperation during this transition.
Hannah Lowe

documents.title: Harbor Maritime Museum: Visitor Information
documents.text:
Hours: Tuesday to Sunday, 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. (closed Mondays, except holidays). Last entry is one hour before closing.

Admission: Adults $14; seniors (65 and over) $10; students with valid ID $8; children under 6 free. Members enter free. On the first Sunday of every month, admission is half price for everyone.

Guided tours: Offered daily at 11 a.m. and 2 p.m. in English and, on weekends, in Spanish. Tours last 45 minutes and are included in the price of admission. Groups of ten or more must book at least two weeks in advance by calling 555-0199.

Visitors may not use flash photography in the exhibition halls. The café on the ground floor is open during regular museum hours.

questions.explanation: The museum closes at 5 p.m. and the last entry is one hour before closing.

choices: Guided tours require an extra payment

questions.explanation: Tours are included in the price of admission.

documents.title: Riverside Launches Bike-Share Program
documents.text: RIVERSIDE (June 3) - The city council announced yesterday that a bike-share program will begin operating on July 1. [A] Residents will be able to rent one of 400 bicycles from 45 stations located near train stations, parks, and shopping areas. [B] The first thirty minutes of each ride will be free, and after that the fee will be $2 per hour. Monthly passes will cost $18. [C] Mayor Diane Okafor said the project aims to reduce traffic downtown and encourage healthy habits, but some business owners have expressed concern that the stations may take up valuable parking spaces. [D] The council will review the program after six months and consider adding stations in the northern suburbs if ridership is high enough.

documents.title: Letter of recommendation
documents.text:
Dear Hiring Committee,
I am pleased to recommend Jonas Weber for the Senior Accountant position at Delta Finance. Mr. Weber worked under my supervision at Calloway Tools for six years, first as a junior accountant and later as team leader. During that time he introduced a new invoicing system that reduced payment errors by 40 percent. He is careful, reliable, and an excellent mentor to younger colleagues. Although he is reserved in large meetings, he communicates clearly in writing and one-on-one. He left Calloway Tools only because the company moved its headquarters to another country. I recommend him without reservation.
Sincerely,
Maria Costa
Finance Director, Calloway Tools

documents.title: Library to Reduce Weekend Hours
documents.text: LANSDALE (October 9) - Starting November 1, the Lansdale Public Library will close at 2 p.m. on Saturdays instead of 6 p.m. and will no longer open on Sundays. Library director Paul Mercer attributed the change to a 12 percent cut in the city's cultural budget. "We regret this decision, but we must protect our programs for children and our digital services," he said. Weekday hours will not change. The library will also reduce the number of new books purchased each year. Residents can comment on the plan at the city council meeting on October 23.

documents.title: Don't cut our library hours
documents.text:
To the Editor:
I was disappointed to read that the Lansdale Public Library will cut its weekend hours. As a nurse who works Monday through Friday, I can only bring my two children to the library on weekends. My son's reading has improved dramatically thanks to the Saturday story hour. I agree that digital services and children's programs are important, but many working families depend on weekend access. I plan to speak at the council meeting on October 23 and encourage other parents to do the same.
Sincerely,
Amy Chen, Lansdale
